headline: Car bomb at Colombia toll booth injures three

sources.title: Car bomb at Colombia toll booth injures three as clashes between the army and rebel groups intensify (AP News)
Ataque con carro bomba dejó tres heridos y provocó cierre de vía Panamericana en Colombia (Primicias)
Carro bomba destruyó peaje de El Bordo, en Cauca: reportan tres civiles heridos y daños en viviendas (Noticias RCN)

chunks.text: On October 12, 2026, a car bomb {{went off}} at a [[toll booth]] on a highway in southwestern Colombia. The army said at least three [[civilians]] were injured. The [[blast]] destroyed the toll booth and damaged nearby homes. Officials {{shut down}} part of the highway. The army blamed a group led by former members of Colombia's largest [[rebel]] army. These fighters did not {{go along with}} the 2016 [[peace deal]].

chunks.text: Colombia's president [[condemned]] the attack on social media. He said attacks on [[infrastructure]] hurt truck drivers and everyone who needs to travel. He took office in August 2026, and his government has {{called off}} peace talks with the country's [[remaining]] rebel groups. He has promised to {{crack down}} on these groups, which he says he will treat as [[terrorists]]. Some groups have {{hit back}} by {{stepping up}} attacks on the military.

verbs.correct: To attack an enemy that attacked you

verbs.why: When rebels attack a village, soldiers usually hit back. Gangs often hit back after police raids. Some rebel groups have hit back by attacking the military.
Cities step up police patrols downtown during the holidays. Airports step up security before Thanksgiving. Some rebel groups have been stepping up attacks on the military.

chunks.text: The bombing came during a [[wave of violence]] in the region. On October 9, the army said the same group killed a soldier in a [[clash]]. The next day, a drone attack killed another soldier. The army said a different rebel group {{carried out}} that attack. In September, the army {{sent in}} troops to a Caribbean city after a drug gang burned vehicles. The president has also {{set up}} a [[task force]] to stop a group from stealing fuel from a [[pipeline]].

verbs.correct: To do something that was planned
verbs.wrong: To deny an attack in public
verbs.why: Nurses carry out the tests in one morning. Workers carry out repairs on the bridge every spring. The army said a different rebel group carried out the drone attack.

verbs.correct: To order troops or police to go to a place
verbs.wrong: To pay troops or police more money
verbs.why: Governors send in soldiers after a big flood. The city sends in more police when a crowd grows. In September, the army sent in troops to a Caribbean city.

verbs.correct: To start a new group or system
verbs.why: Many schools set up clubs for new students. Some towns set up teams to clean their rivers. The president has set up a task force to protect a fuel pipeline.

chunks.text: The president's policies are a big change. The previous government spent four years trying to [[negotiate]] with rebel groups. In 2016, about 14,000 fighters {{laid down}} their weapons after the peace deal. But the deal left some [[rural areas]] without strong government control. Smaller armed groups have tried to {{take over}} land the old rebel army once held. They fight for control of gold mines and [[drug routes]], and they [[demand]] money from local businesses.

verbs.wrong: To sell weapons to other groups
verbs.why: Soldiers lay down their guns when they surrender. Rebels lay down their weapons after a peace deal. In 2016, about 14,000 fighters laid down their weapons after the peace deal.

verbs.wrong: To plant crops in a place
verbs.why: Rebels sometimes take over radio stations during a war. Protesters take over the main square in many big protests. Smaller armed groups have tried to take over land that the old rebel army once held.

mainIdea.s: A car bomb at a highway toll booth in Colombia injured at least three people, and the army blamed former rebels. Attacks are rising after the government ended peace talks with rebel groups.
mainIdea.why: A car bomb went off at a toll booth, and the army blamed former rebels. The government has called off peace talks, and some groups have stepped up attacks.

mainIdea.s: Three people were hurt when a bomb exploded at a Colombian toll station, and the group responsible quickly apologized. The president now plans to restart peace talks with every armed group.
mainIdea.why: Close, but no group said it was sorry, and the government has called off peace talks. The president has promised to crack down on rebel groups.

mainIdea.s: Colombia has opened a new highway that links its capital to the Caribbean coast. Officials say the road will make trips much shorter and bring more tourists and new jobs to small towns.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a car bomb in Colombia and rising violence after the government called off peace talks with rebel groups.

lines.text: Did you hear about the car bomb in Colombia?
A bomb {{went off}} at a toll booth on a big highway. At least three people were hurt.
That's terrible. Who do they think did it?
The army blamed former rebels who didn't {{go along with}} the 2016 peace deal.
I thought most of the rebels {{laid down}} their weapons years ago.
Most did. But smaller groups have tried to {{take over}} the land they left.
Is the government still talking to them?
No. The president {{called off}} the peace talks. He wants to [[take a hard line]].
So he's going to {{crack down}} on them?
That's the plan. He says he'll treat them as terrorists, so he clearly [[means business]].
Some have {{hit back}} by {{stepping up}} attacks on the army.
More attacks, then more force. It sounds like [[a vicious cycle]].
It's [[a tough call]] for the government. Years of talks didn't stop the violence either.
I just hope people there can feel safe again soon.
